rationale: The analysis correctly identifies the positional mapper indexing as the root cause, with the added optional field as the triggering precondition and the validator as a correctly-functioning surface that surfaces but does not originate the corruption. It explicitly covers all four required findings: positional shift mechanism (C4/C5), validator surfaced but did not originate corruption (C6/C7 plus explicit statement), retries not changing outcome due to determinism (C9), and named-field mapping fixing the sample (C10/A1). Both forbidden claims are explicitly negated: it states the validator behaved correctly (not root cause) and frames the mapper test gap, not partner contract violation, as the defect (C2 explicitly affirms the partner's change was contract-permitted). Causal chain is well-structured and matches evidence directionality without inventing unsupported structure; the C7→C4 relationship is appropriately marked 'unknown'/directional rather than causal, showing good calibration. Evidence discipline is strong — nearly every claim cites specific evidence IDs, and the one low-confidence extrapolation (C12 on the 18% rate) is explicitly flagged as not stated by evidence. Uncertainty section is thorough, surfacing genuinely open questions (schema-level defect alternative, other consumers affected, retention of rejected records) without hiding the core diagnosis's low uncertainty per ground truth. Actions correctly prioritize the mapper fix and test-hardening as primary leverage, explicitly reject weakening the validator, and add reasonable containment/recovery actions without overreach. No harmful actions, no forbidden claims, no unsupported outside-evidence use, and no attempt to identify or reference the analyzer/condition.
